tasks.description: Create a CLAUDE.md file in the project root. phases.name: Core data pipeline implementation
phases.description: Implement git log parsing and commit categorization — the pure functions that transform raw git output into structured, categorized data.

tasks.title: Implement parseGitLog in git.ts
tasks.description: Implement the parseGitLog function in src/git.ts. Split raw input on the COMMIT_SEPARATOR ('---COMMIT---'). For each non-empty block: extract SHA (first line), subject (second line), body (everything between line 3 and '---BODY_END---' marker, trimmed, may be empty), author name (line after ---BODY_END---), author date in ISO format with offset (next line). Then parse --stat output that follows the author date: individual file lines matching the pattern ' path | N +- ' and the summary line ' N files changed, N insertions(+), N deletions(-)'. Build FileStat[] from individual file lines. Parse total insertions/deletions from the summary line. Construct Commit objects with timestamp as Date preserving the original offset string for later use. If a required field is missing, throw with a message identifying the malformed block. Return Commit[]. Also implement readGitLog using spawnSync as shown in the plan S4.
acceptanceCriteria: parseGitLog with three-commit fixture returns array of 3 Commit objects with correct fields
parseGitLog with empty string returns empty array
parseGitLog with malformed block throws with descriptive message
Timestamps preserve timezone offset information
readGitLog throws 'git is not available on PATH' when spawnSync result.error is set
readGitLog throws with repo path and stderr when git exits non-zero

tasks.title: Implement categorize.ts functions
tasks.description: Implement all functions in src/categorize.ts. categorizeCommit(commit: Commit): CategorizedCommit — strip leading whitespace from subject, lowercase it, match against regex ^(feat|fix|refactor|docs|chore|test|style|perf|build|ci)(\(.+\))?: to extract the prefix as CommitCategory. If no match, assign 'other'. extractTilItems(commit: Commit, repoName: string): TilItem[] — scan subject and body for lines containing 'TIL:' (case-sensitive). Extract everything after 'TIL:' to end of line, trim whitespace. Return TilItem with text, repoName, and 7-char short SHA. assignDaySegment(timestamp: Date, tzOffset: string): DaySegment — compute the local hour using the timezone offset embedded in the git timestamp. Map: 5-11 morning, 12-16 afternoon, 17-23 evening, 0-4 night. buildRepoEntry(repoPath: string, commits: Commit[]): RepoEntry — categorize each commit, extract TIL items, assign day segments. Sort commits ascending by timestamp. Use path.basename for repoName. buildDiaryEntry(date: string, repoEntries: RepoEntry[]): DiaryEntry — aggregate TIL items from all repos, deduplicate by exact text match keeping first occurrence.
acceptanceCriteria: categorizeCommit assigns correct category for all 11 prefix types
Category matching is case-insensitive
Scoped prefixes like feat(scope): are recognized
No-prefix subjects get 'other'
extractTilItems finds TIL in subject and body
Multiple TIL items from one commit are all extracted
assignDaySegment maps hours correctly per spec boundaries
buildDiaryEntry deduplicates TIL items by text

phases.name: Markdown generation and file I/O
phases.description: Implement markdown rendering from structured diary data and filesystem operations for reading/writing diary files.

tasks.title: Implement markdown.ts
tasks.description: Implement all functions in src/markdown.ts. formatDiaryEntry(entry: DiaryEntry): string — generate markdown following spec BR-8 format. Start with '## YYYY-MM-DD' heading. If tilItems is non-empty, add '### Today I Learned' section with items formatted as '- Item text (`abc1234`, repo-name)'. For each repo in entry.repos (in order), add '### repo-name' heading. List commits flat, sorted ascending by timestamp, formatted as '- `<short-sha>` <subject> — <category> (+<insertions> / -<deletions>)'. Short SHA is first 7 characters. If all repos have zero commits, return empty string. findExistingEntry(content: string, date: string): boolean — scan content for a line matching '## YYYY-MM-DD' (the date heading). Return true if found. replaceEntry(content: string, date: string, newEntry: string): string — find the existing entry block (from its ## heading to the line before the next ## heading or end of file), remove it, insert newEntry at the same position. appendEntry(content: string | null, date: string, newEntry: string): string — if content is null, create new file with '# Code Diary — YYYY-MM' top heading followed by newEntry and trailing '---'. If content exists, append '---' separator and newEntry to end.

All imports from 'fs' and 'path' (for dirname).

phases.name: CLI wiring and entry point
phases.description: Implement argument parsing, input validation, the replace prompt, and the top-level orchestration that ties all modules together.

tasks.title: Implement cli.ts argument parsing and validation
tasks.description: Implement src/cli.ts. parseArgs(argv: string[]): CliArgs — parse process.argv (slice off first 2 elements). Collect positional args as repoPaths, extract --date and --output flags. If no repoPaths, write usage to stderr and exit(2). Default date to today via new Date().toLocaleDateString('en-CA'). Validate date with isValidDate helper: must match /^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/ and be a valid calendar date; if invalid exit(2) with error message. Default outputDir to process.cwd(). Export CliArgs type. validateRepoPaths(paths: string[]): void — for each path, resolve to absolute, check existsSync (exit 2 with 'path does not exist'), check existsSync(join(abs, '.git')) (exit 2 with 'not a git repository'). Implement promptReplace using readline from node:readline as shown in plan S5. Implement run(argv: string[]): Promise<void> as the top-level orchestrator: parseArgs → validateRepoPaths → for each repo call readGitLog and parseGitLog → buildRepoEntry → filter empty → if none exit 0 with message → buildDiaryEntry → formatDiaryEntry → check existing entry → prompt if needed → writeFile. Handle the replace flow per spec §2 and FM-8.
acceptanceCriteria: parseArgs extracts repo paths, date, and output correctly
Missing repo paths triggers exit(2) with usage message
Invalid date triggers exit(2) with error message
validateRepoPaths checks existence and .git presence
Non-interactive stdin skips prompt and exits 1
run orchestrates the full pipeline correctly
